scenario: Wazuh SIEM Living-off-the-Land (LotL) Attack with In-Memory PowerShell, SAM Dump, WMI Persistence, and C2 Exfiltration
summary: On 2026-10-15, an adversary executed a multi-stage Living-off-the-Land attack across WS-DEV-01 (Agent ID 001) and WS-ADMIN-01 (Agent ID 002). The attacker leveraged hidden in-memory PowerShell (PID 4512) to enumerate local administrators, access the SAM registry hive, and inspect LSASS process handles. The adversary established WMI event consumer persistence, staged credentials in C:\Temp\credentials.txt, connected to C2 infrastructure (attacker.com:80 and 198.51.100.45:4444), moved laterally via SMB to 10.10.2.51, and exfiltrated data to exfil.attacker.com.
kill_chain: 08:05 powershell.exe -NoP -W Hidden invoked on WS-DEV-01 (user developer)
08:06 SAM hive discovery via Get-ItemProperty HKLM:\SAM
08:15 Credential inspection via LSASS process handle request
08:20 Outbound C2 beaconing to attacker.com (port 80) and registry Run key persistence
09:05 Lateral movement probing from 10.10.2.50 to 10.10.2.51 via RPC (port 135) and SMB (port 445)
09:20 Staging stolen credentials to C:\Temp\credentials.txt and clipboard.txt
10:00 Exfiltration of staged data to exfil.attacker.com
evidence_basis: registry_access (SAM hive discovery and registry persistence)
